title: GitHub Copilot License: Plans, Seat Prices and AI Credits

facts.fact: GitHub's published price for Copilot Pro (individual plan) is $10 USD per month, with 1,500 AI credits per month (1,000 base + 500 flex), according to the LICENSEWARE wiki's table.
facts.quote: Copilot Pro | Individual | $10 USD per month | 1,500 (1,000 base + 500 flex)

facts.fact: GitHub's published price for Copilot Pro+ (individual plan) is $39 USD per month, with 7,000 AI credits per month (3,900 base + 3,100 flex).
facts.quote: Copilot Pro+ | Individual | $39 USD per month | 7,000 (3,900 base + 3,100 flex)

facts.fact: GitHub's published price for Copilot Max (individual plan) is $100 USD per month, with 20,000 AI credits per month (10,000 base + 10,000 flex).
facts.quote: Copilot Max | Individual | $100 USD per month | 20,000 (10,000 base + 10,000 flex)

facts.fact: GitHub's published price for Copilot Business is $19 USD per granted seat per month, with 1,900 AI credits per user pooled.
facts.unit: USD per granted seat per month
facts.quote: Copilot Business | Organizations and enterprises | $19 USD per granted seat per month | 1,900 per user, pooled

facts.fact: GitHub's published price for Copilot Enterprise (Enterprise Cloud) is $39 USD per granted seat per month, with 3,900 AI credits per user pooled.
facts.unit: USD per granted seat per month
facts.quote: Copilot Enterprise | Enterprises on GitHub Enterprise Cloud | $39 USD per granted seat per month | 3,900 per user, pooled

facts.fact: GitHub states that 1 AI credit equals $0.01 USD.
facts.quote: 1 AI credit equals $0.01 USD.

facts.fact: GitHub lists seven Copilot plans: Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise.
facts.quote: GitHub lists seven Copilot plans. Copilot is not currently available for GitHub Enterprise Server.

facts.fact: Copilot Free and Copilot Student include an AI credit allowance, but the amount is not stated in GitHub's plan documentation.
facts.quote: Copilot Free | Individual | Free | An allowance (amount not stated)

facts.fact: Copilot Pro is free for verified teachers and maintainers of popular open source projects.
facts.quote: Copilot Pro is free for verified teachers and maintainers of popular open source projects

facts.fact: GitHub defines a Copilot seat as a license to use Copilot, assigned to a unique user account through a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise plan.
facts.quote: GitHub defines a seat as a license to use Copilot, assigned to a unique user account through a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise plan.

facts.fact: Organizations and enterprises are billed for the number of assigned Copilot seats at the end of each monthly billing cycle.
facts.quote: Organizations and enterprises are billed for the number of assigned seats at the end of each monthly billing cycle.

facts.fact: A user who holds both a Copilot Business seat and a Copilot Enterprise seat is billed only for the Enterprise seat, at the Enterprise rate from the time it was assigned.
facts.quote: If a user holds both a Business and an Enterprise seat, only the Enterprise seat is billed, at the Enterprise rate from the time it was assigned.

facts.fact: Seats added mid-cycle are billed for the rest of the cycle, prorated by the date added, and GitHub issues no refunds for unused time.
facts.quote: Seats added mid-cycle are billed for the rest of the cycle, prorated by the date added.

facts.fact: Removed Copilot seats stop billing at the end of the cycle, and an unassigned user keeps access until the cycle ends while a revoked seat loses access immediately.
facts.quote: Removed seats stop billing at the end of the cycle, the lower count applies from the next cycle, and GitHub issues no refunds for unused time.

facts.fact: When a Pro, Pro+ or Max subscriber is assigned a Business or Enterprise seat, the personal plan is canceled automatically with a prorated refund.
facts.quote: When a Pro, Pro+ or Max subscriber is assigned a Business or Enterprise seat, the personal plan is canceled automatically with a prorated refund.

facts.fact: Removing every assigned seat from an organization cancels the organization's Copilot plan.
facts.quote: removing every assigned seat cancels the organization’s Copilot plan.

facts.fact: For Business and Enterprise, each assigned license adds its included AI credits to a pool at billing entity level; 100 Copilot Business users give a shared pool of 190,000 credits.
facts.quote: 100 Copilot Business users give a shared pool of 190,000 credits.

facts.fact: Unused AI credits are forfeited, and the allowance resets at 00:00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month, regardless of the subscription billing date.
facts.quote: In both cases unused credits are forfeited, and the allowance resets at 00:00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month, whatever the subscription billing date.

facts.fact: Paid personal Copilot plans consume base AI credits first, then a variable flex allotment that GitHub says is designed to adapt as the economics of AI evolve.
facts.quote: Paid personal plans consume base credits first, then a variable flex allotment that GitHub says is designed to adapt as the economics of AI evolve.

facts.fact: GitHub's current documentation meters Copilot usage in AI credits, and the retrieved plan and billing pages show no premium request allowance, although the pricing page still names a legacy 'Premium request paid usage' policy.
facts.quote: The pricing page still names a legacy “Premium request paid usage” policy, but no premium request allowance appears in the retrieved plan or billing pages

facts.fact: With GitHub Enterprise Cloud, an enterprise owner chooses Business or Enterprise for each organization, so both plans can coexist in one enterprise.
facts.quote: an enterprise owner chooses Business or Enterprise for each organization, so both plans can coexist in one enterprise.

facts.fact: GitHub Copilot Free includes 2000 code completions per month.
facts.quote: Copilot Free includes 2000 code completions per month.

facts.fact: Code completions and next edit suggestions are not billed in AI credits and stay unlimited on paid plans.
facts.quote: Code completions and next edit suggestions are not billed in AI credits and stay unlimited on paid plans.

facts.fact: Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise are both billed monthly per granted seat.
facts.quote: Copilot Business** and **Copilot Enterprise**: both billed monthly per granted seat.

facts.fact: Copilot Enterprise is designed for enterprises using GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
facts.quote: Copilot Enterprise is designed for enterprises using GitHub Enterprise Cloud.

facts.fact: Individual Copilot plans are tied to a single account and cannot carry additional seats, so licensing several users requires an organization plan.
facts.quote: Individual plans are tied to a single account and cannot carry additional seats; licensing several users needs an organization plan.

facts.fact: Purchasing additional AI credits is not available for Copilot plans bought through GitHub Mobile on iOS or Android.
facts.quote: Purchasing additional AI credits is not available for plans bought through GitHub Mobile on iOS or Android.

facts.fact: Copilot Business and Enterprise bought directly from GitHub fall under the GitHub Generative AI Services Terms, purchases through Microsoft fall under Microsoft's Product Terms, and all other users fall under Section J of the GitHub Terms of Service.
facts.quote: Business and Enterprise bought directly from GitHub fall under the GitHub Generative AI Services Terms; purchases through Microsoft fall under Microsoft’s Product Terms; all other users fall under Section J of the GitHub Terms of Service.

facts.fact: The GitHub Generative AI Services Terms state that GitHub will not use Inputs or Outputs to train generative AI models unless the customer has given documented instructions.
facts.quote: The Generative AI Services Terms state that GitHub will not use Inputs or Outputs to train generative AI models unless the customer has given documented instructions.

facts.fact: For individual licenses, Section J.3 of the GitHub Terms of Service grants GitHub a license to use Inputs and Outputs to develop and train AI models unless the user opts out in account settings or is covered by a customer or volume licensing agreement.
facts.quote: For individual licenses, Section J.3 grants GitHub a license to use Inputs and Outputs to develop and train AI models unless the user opts out in account settings or is covered by a customer or volume licensing agreement.

facts.fact: For individual Copilot plans, upgrades take effect immediately with proration, downgrades apply from the next cycle, and cancelling a monthly plan keeps access until the cycle ends.
facts.quote: upgrades take effect immediately with proration; downgrades apply from the next cycle; cancelling a monthly plan keeps access until the cycle ends.

facts.fact: Once the Copilot AI credit pool is exhausted, additional usage continues at per-token model rates converted to AI credits (pay-as-you-go).
facts.quote: once the pool is exhausted, usage continues at per-token model rates converted to AI credits.

facts.fact: Copilot additional usage budgets can be set per user, cost center, organization and enterprise.
facts.quote: Budgets can be set per user, cost center, organization and enterprise;

facts.fact: A user who exhausts a user-level Copilot budget is blocked even if the pool still has capacity.
facts.quote: a user who exhausts a user-level budget is blocked even if the pool still has capacity.

facts.fact: The GitHub Terms of Service Section J (AI Features, Training, and Your Data) is effective from 2026-04-27, per the cited reference.
facts.quote: Effective 2026-04-27. Retrieved 2026-10-07.

facts.fact: The GitHub Generative AI Services Terms cited on this page are Version: March 2026.
facts.quote: GitHub Generative AI Services Terms (Version: March 2026)

facts.fact: The page's reference list states that GitHub Copilot is not available for GitHub Enterprise Server, citing GitHub's plans documentation.
facts.quote: Plan descriptions, prices, AI credit allowances; GitHub Enterprise Server exclusion.
